title: When the Wolf Breaks Revisited
premise: Juniper Okonkwo has spent their whole life guarding the Hollow Gate, the sealed mountain pass that keeps the old magic of Thornfell from spilling into the lowlands. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into their hands, Juniper discovers the Gate was never meant to keep magic out — it was meant to keep a bound king in, and the seal is failing. Guided by the map and joined by an unlikely found family of smugglers, exiles, and one very stubborn wolf-spirit, Juniper must reach the buried court beneath the mountains before the thing wearing the king's crown breaks free. In the end, Juniper learns that unbinding the king means choosing between duty to the Gate and love for the people they've gathered along the way — and they choose both, sacrificing the Gate itself to forge a new covenant where belonging, not imprisonment, holds the old magic in check.
about_author: Oscar Coldharbour is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders, doors, and the people who decide which side of them to stand on.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Round
chapters.summary: Juniper Okonkwo walks the nightly circuit of the Hollow Gate, checking seals only they can hear humming. POV: Juniper. Establishes their solitary routine, their pride in the duty inherited from their grandmother, and the first faint wrongness: the Gate's hum has gone flat on the north face.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Threshold
chapters.summary: A courier staggers out of the storm with arrow wounds and a wax-sealed map tube, dying on Juniper's floor. With her last breath she says 'the king is awake' and begs Juniper to carry it to someone called the Ashwife. POV: Juniper. The beat is shock — the first death Juniper has ever witnessed inside the Gate.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Juniper opens the map and finds routes through Thornfell no living person should know — including passages under the Gate itself. Their grandmother's journals confirm fragments. POV: Juniper, with journal excerpts. The emotional beat is disillusionment: the duty they loved may be built on lies.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Welcome
chapters.summary: To follow the map, Juniper needs guides, so they seek Wren Halloway, a smuggler who owes Juniper a debt from a border arrest. Wren agrees — for a price — and brings her crew: gruff ferryman Doss and runaway scholar Tam. POV: Wren. The beat is wary negotiation sparking mutual respect.

chapters.title: Down the Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: The company travels the hidden roads; Juniper realizes their knowledge of every path makes them the group's true guide, not passenger. An ambush by crown soldiers hunting the map forces their first fight. POV: Tam. The beat is found-family beginnings forged under fire.

chapters.title: The Wolf on the Ridge
chapters.summary: A huge grey wolf shadows the party for days before speaking — it is Vael, a spirit bound to the old king, who claims the map leads to his master's prison. It offers truth in exchange for passage. POV: Juniper. The beat is temptation versus suspicion.

chapters.title: The Ashwife's Hearth
chapters.summary: They reach the Ashwife, an exiled court-magician living in a burned watchtower with a household of strays. She reads the map and confirms the worst: the binding on King Aldric is unraveling, and the thing wearing his crown — the Hollow Regent — will be free by midwinter. POV: the Ashwife. The beat is dread made concrete, plus warmth of her chaotic household.

chapters.title: Three Ways Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: The map shows three approaches to the buried court; each demands something terrible. The company argues over the route while scouts report the Regent's agents — hollow-eyed men — sweeping the passes. POV: Wren. The beat is fracture: Wren wants to walk away, but can't abandon them.

chapters.title: The Drowned Stair
chapters.summary: They take the river route through flooded caverns. Doss pilots them through collapsing tunnels; Tam nearly drowns saving the map, and Juniper pulls him out. POV: Tam. The beat is terror transformed into trust — Tam stops being the outsider.

chapters.title: Hollow Eyes
chapters.summary: The Regent's agents ambush the camp at night. In the fight, Juniper touches one and sees through its eyes: the buried court, the crowned figure on a throne of roots, waiting. POV: Juniper. The beat is horror and a terrible intimacy with the enemy.

chapters.title: Vael's Confession
chapters.summary: Vael admits it helped bind the king originally — and that the binding required a willing heart, which is why the Regent now needs Juniper, a keeper, to complete its escape. POV: Vael (rendered as close third). The beat is betrayal reframed as penance.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Crown soldiers capture Wren and Doss, offering freedom for the map. Wren burns her own smuggling ledger instead, destroying her old life to protect the company. POV: Wren. The beat is sacrifice — she chooses the found family over survival.

chapters.title: The Rescue at Cold Ford
chapters.summary: Juniper, Tam, and Vael assault the ford garrison using smugglers' tricks and the wolf's strength. They free Wren and Doss, but Juniper is wounded and fevered. POV: alternating Juniper/Wren. The beat is the family fighting as one, at real cost.

chapters.title: Fever Dreams of the First Keeper
chapters.summary: Delirious, Juniper dreams their grandmother's memories stored in the Gate: the original binding, the young king who volunteered, the lie told to all keepers since. POV: dream-Juniper. The beat is understanding — duty was always meant to end here, with a choice.

chapters.title: Midwinter Closes In
chapters.summary: The company races the last stretch as snow seals the high passes behind them — no retreat. The Ashwife's messenger arrives with a final warning: the Regent has begun calling Juniper by name in its sleep. POV: Doss. The beat is point of no return, quiet courage in the ordinary man.

chapters.title: The Court of Roots
chapters.summary: They descend into the buried court: a vast hall of living wood where King Aldric sits enthroned, half himself, half Hollow. He recognizes Vael and weeps. The Regent rises from the throne's shadow to greet Juniper like an old friend. POV: Juniper. The beat is awe curdling into confrontation.

chapters.title: The Bargain of the Crown
chapters.summary: The Regent offers Juniper everything: safety for their friends, restoration of the Gate, even their grandmother back — if they willingly rebind the king forever, sealing themselves in too. Aldric, lucid for a moment, begs instead to be released to die. POV: Juniper. The beat is the central choice laid bare.

chapters.title: What the Family Decides
chapters.summary: Juniper refuses to choose alone; the company speaks — Wren's defiance, Tam's scholarship finding the flaw in the binding, Doss's plain decency, Vael's offer to take the king's place. Together they craft a third answer neither duty nor the Regent imagined. POV: multiple voices. The beat is found family as the story's true magic.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: In the climax, Tam unravels the binding's grammar while Vael channels the king's curse into itself; the Regent fights them with stolen memories and hollow soldiers. Juniper must hold the Gate-hum alone, singing the counter-song their grandmother left hidden in the map. POV: Juniper. The beat is climax — everyone giving everything at once.

chapters.title: The Wolf Breaks
chapters.summary: Vael takes the Regent into itself and shatters, freeing Aldric, who dies human and grateful in the spring thaw light. The Gate cracks open above as its purpose ends. Juniper grieves the wolf and the grandmother's lie together. POV: Juniper. The beat is grief and release intertwined.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.summary: With the Gate fallen, magic and lowlands meet openly; the company helps negotiate the Accord of Thornfell, with the Ashwife as envoy and Aldric's heir as witness. Juniper is offered the keepership reborn — and declines it. POV: Wren. The beat is the world remade by ordinary hands.

chapters.title: Home Is the Road We Walk Together
chapters.summary: Spring on the mountain: Juniper builds a waystation at the old Gate site, not to bar travelers but to welcome them. Wren, Tam, and Doss drift back each season; Vael's pawprint remains in the stone. Juniper finally belongs — not to a gate, but to people. POV: Juniper. The beat is resolution and warm, earned peace.
